title: Phase 1 market-baseline probability comparison for KXBTC 60-second averaged terminal ranges

source_selection_branches.implied: feature_recipe.selected_volatility_kind is implied: an admissible matching-interval DVOL implied volatility was selected by ResearchContext.to_crypto_snapshot
source_selection_branches.realized: feature_recipe.selected_volatility_kind is realized: no admissible matching-interval implied volatility, so the realized_window_seconds realized volatility at realized_interval_seconds was selected
source_selection_branches.identity: each distinct (selected_volatility_kind, selected_volatility_provider, selected_volatility_window_seconds, recipe_id) is a separate predeclared branch identity, reported with its own row, event and date counts and descriptive point metrics; branches are pooled only because they follow the one fixed selection rule, are never collapsed into a single recipe identity, and never select the population or the conclusion

source_kinds.synthetic-fixture: Declarative synthetic observations run through the real engine; never empirical evidence.
source_kinds.retrospective-local: Previously recorded forward-evaluation ledger rows inside the archive window; already-seen local evidence, never untouched.
source_kinds.forward-holdout: Forward-evaluation rows with decision time inside the holdout window, recorded before outcomes existed; not implemented in Phase 1 and never inferred from retrospective provenance.

timestamp_rules: Every timestamp MUST be ISO 8601 with an explicit UTC offset and is normalized to UTC; naive or unparseable timestamps exclude the observation (reason: invalid_timestamp).
Decision time is opportunity.market.observed_at; opportunity.forecast.generated_at MUST equal it (reason: forecast_time_mismatch).
All windows are half-open [start, end) in UTC and are applied to decision time.

Event date is the UTC calendar date of the explicit opportunity.market.observation_end_at; every observation of one event MUST share that date, otherwise the whole event is excluded (reason: event_date_conflict) rather than being counted as more than one independent event.
Fold membership uses decision time; an event whose observations span two folds is assigned to the fold containing its earliest decision time.
availability_rules: Only information available at decision time is admissible: inputs.crypto.observed_at <= decision time and all research-context source availability/retrieval times <= decision time (reason: future_input).
Crypto input age at decision (market.observed_at - crypto.observed_at) MUST be within [0, maximum_input_age_seconds] (reason: stale_input or future_input). Synthetic fixtures do not bypass this.

retrospective-local rows MUST carry a complete content-addressed research context whose content_id equals inputs.crypto.input_provenance.research_context_id, whose spot_end_at equals inputs.crypto.observed_at, and which passes ResearchContext.validate_at(decision time, maximum_input_age_seconds) (reason: research_context_unavailable or research_context_invalid). Legacy rows lacking provenance are excluded, never reconstructed as point-in-time.
synthetic-fixture rows MAY use manual features only when explicitly labelled synthetic; freshness and timing rules still apply.
run_manifest_sha256 MUST equal content_id(run_manifest) and input_id MUST equal content_id(inputs) (reason: identity_mismatch).

retrospective-local rows MUST be evidence class forward-evaluation; historical-evaluation, manual-evaluation and ambiguous-legacy rows are excluded (reason: evidence_class). Source provenance never fabricates a forward class.

A calibration profile recorded in inputs.calibration_profile is compatible only if symbol, model_name, model_version and recipe_id match the forecast, training_start >= protocol training_start, cutoff_at <= min(training_end, decision time), and independent_event_count >= minimum_calibration_events. An incompatible or temporally invalid recorded profile excludes the row (reason: calibration_profile_invalid). Rows with no profile (uncertainty_source fixed) remain eligible; calibration affects only the uncertainty interval and recommendation, never the scored probabilities.

An outcome is known only if resolution.result is yes or no and resolution.observed_at <= report as_of; otherwise the row is unresolved (retained, unscored). A resolution observed at or before decision time excludes the row (reason: outcome_leak).
eligibility_rules: opportunity.market.series_id equals series and inputs.crypto.symbol equals symbol (reason: out_of_scope).
inputs.contract is a terminal range: 0 < lower_bound < upper_bound and settlement_window_seconds equals settlement_window_seconds (reason: unsupported_contract).

forecast.model_name equals model_name exactly, forecast.model_version equals model_version, inputs.recipe.structural_weight and inputs.engine_config.structural_weight equal structural_weight, and forecast.recipe_id equals the fingerprint of inputs.recipe (reason: model_mismatch).

Production rows (retrospective-local, forward-holdout): inputs.recipe.expected_annual_return and inputs.crypto.expected_annual_return equal expected_annual_return; inputs.crypto.feature_recipe equals inputs.recipe.features; every production_features key equals the same key in feature_recipe; and the research context reproduces them (spot.interval_seconds, realized_volatility.raw_payload.interval_seconds, realized_volatility.window_seconds) plus the selected volatility kind, provider and window of ResearchContext.to_crypto_snapshot (reason: feature_recipe_mismatch). optional_max_age_seconds is recorded, not pinned.
synthetic-fixture rows are exempt from the production feature-recipe rule only when explicitly labelled synthetic, and are never pooled with production rows.
opportunity.market.event_id is an explicit non-empty venue event identifier; no fallback to market_id or contract label (reason: missing_event_id).
opportunity.market.observation_end_at is explicit; observation_start_at is null or equals observation_end_at - settlement_window_seconds (reason: missing_observation_provenance).

Decision time is at or before observation_end_at - settlement_window_seconds (averaging has not begun) and min(expires_at, observation_end_at) - decision time >= minimum_seconds_to_entry_horizon (reason: timing_ineligible).
market.yes_ask is present, finite and in [0, 1] with yes_ask_size present and >= minimum_ask_size (reason: no_displayed_ask).

All present quotes are finite in [0, 1] with yes_bid <= yes_ask and no_bid <= no_ask; structural, blend and recorded midpoint probabilities are finite in [0, 1] and lower_probability_yes <= probability_yes <= upper_probability_yes (reason: invalid_quote or invalid_arm). A missing or invalid arm excludes the entire row, never one arm.
Decision time lies inside the window of the source kind: archive window and before report_as_of for retrospective-local; holdout window for forward-holdout (reason: outside_window).

Duplicate observation_id values, checked across every input observation (adapter-excluded rows included) before any other rule: if every copy has identical content_id(observation), exactly one copy is kept and the others are excluded (reason: duplicate_observation); if any copies disagree, ALL copies with that observation_id are excluded (reason: duplicate_conflict). The result never depends on input order.
Every recommendation state (WATCH included) is eligible; no selection on entry, edge or recommendation state.
unsupported_rules: Threshold (above/below) and touch-barrier contracts are outside the terminal-range family.
Ranges without positive strictly increasing bounds, without an explicit fixed-time terminal observation, or with touch semantics are unsupported.
Settlement averaging other than explicit simple arithmetic averaging of the 60 seconds before observation end (weighted, geometric, median, other windows, ambiguous wording) is unsupported.
Non-binary markets, non-$1 payouts, inactive markets, metadata from the future, conflicting observation clocks and elapsed averaging prefixes are unsupported.
Unsupported rows are listed in the excluded output with reason; they are never approximated or silently dropped.

metrics.brier: (p - y)^2 with y = 1 for yes, 0 for no
metrics.scored_population: resolved eligible rows with all three arms valid; unresolved eligible rows are retained in observations and coverage but unscored
metrics.event_weighting: average the metric over the scored rows of each event, then average event scores with equal weight; repeated contracts or timestamps never increase the independent event count
metrics.paired_delta: per-event mean of arm A minus per-event mean of arm B, averaged over events; negative favours arm A
metrics.secondary_baseline: recorded_midpoint_anchor is the engine's log-odds market anchor from bid/ask midpoints; it is descriptive only, reported separately, and is NOT an executable price
metrics.calibration: per arm, calibration_bins equal-width bins on [0, 1] (last bin closed); each scored row weighted 1 / number of scored rows in its event; each bin emits forecast_count, event_count, weight_sum, weighted mean probability and weighted mean outcome
metrics.coverage: counts of eligible rows/events, resolved/unresolved rows/events, excluded rows by reason, recommendation-state mix, distinct event dates, qualifying folds

bootstrap.generator: Python standard-library random.Random(bootstrap_seed); clusters sorted by stable identifier (event_id, or ISO date) before sampling
bootstrap.interval: percentile interval at (1 - confidence) / 2 and 1 - (1 - confidence) / 2
bootstrap.primary: event cluster bootstrap: resample scored events with replacement, statistic = mean of sampled event scores
bootstrap.secondary: UTC event-date block bootstrap: resample event dates with replacement, include every scored event of each sampled date, statistic = sum of sampled event scores / sampled event count
bootstrap.pairing: the same resample index sets are applied to every arm and every paired difference within a replicate
bootstrap.degenerate: fewer than two clusters yields a null interval, not zero width

regimes.source: opportunity.market_regime price_trend and volatility at decision time; missing is 'unknown'; never inferred from outcomes
regimes.use: descriptive only: per-regime point metrics with row, event and date counts; no intervals or bootstrap for any regime, because regimes are few categories and not independent clusters; regimes never select the population or the conclusion

fold_rules: A validation or holdout fold qualifies when it contains at least minimum_fold_resolved_events scored events.
At least minimum_validation_folds qualifying folds are required before any directional statement; missing qualifying calibration or holdout folds are explicit limitations.
Training and validation windows constrain which existing calibration evidence may be recorded; they do not assert that such evidence exists or was fitted.
cost_rules: decision_costs, cost_scenarios and execution apply only to Phase 1C paper decision analysis after Phase 1B is complete; they never alter probability metrics or eligibility.
minimum_ask_size (top level) gates baseline eligibility; decision_costs.minimum_ask_size is recorded engine policy and does not re-gate recorded engine states.
The execution side is the engine's chosen YES or NO side and fills use that side's actual later ask and displayed size, as defined in execution.

The fill snapshot is the first snapshot at or after decision time + latency_seconds, no later than maximum_input_age_seconds after that instant and no later than min(expires_at, observation_end_at) - minimum_seconds_to_expiry; otherwise nonfill.
Every scenario is reported, and conclusions use the most adverse reported scenario.
tuning_policy: No fitting, tuning, threshold search or model selection is performed under this protocol. Engine 2.1.0 with structural_weight 0.5 is fixed; all constants above were chosen before any outcome was read.
training_claim: This protocol makes no claim that training, calibration or validation data exist or were fitted; any calibration evidence is used only if recorded, temporally valid and compatible.
outcome_access: Frozen before any local database read and before any outcome was inspected; superseded v1 was never used.
conclusion_rules: synthetic-fixture results are always 'inconclusive' and are pipeline demonstrations only.
retrospective-local results are always 'inconclusive' for any unseen-event claim, regardless of point estimate, p-value or interval sign; they are already-seen local evidence.
forward-holdout results are 'inconclusive' unless scored events >= minimum_resolved_events, distinct event dates >= minimum_dates, and qualifying holdout folds >= minimum_validation_folds.

When those minima hold, a directional statement for a paired difference requires both the event bootstrap and the date-block bootstrap intervals to exclude zero in the same direction for both Brier and log loss; otherwise 'inconclusive'.
Low events or dates, missing qualifying calibration or holdout folds, and unresolved or excluded coverage are always listed as limitations.
Probability evidence and paper decisions are reported separately; decisions wait for Phase 1B completion.
replacement_policy: This file is immutable once any analysis has used it. Any change to eligibility, metrics, windows or constants requires a new protocol_version, a new file path and a new protocol_id, plus an explicit trial record; v1 and v2 are preserved unchanged.
protocol_id_rule: protocol_id = 'sha256:' + content_id(every top-level field except protocol_id), where content_id is sha256 of json.dumps(sort_keys=True, separators=(',', ':'), allow_nan=False) as in prediction_market_system.evidence.

execution.applies_to: Phase 1C paper decisions only, after Phase 1B is complete; never alters probability metrics or eligibility
execution.entry: only rows whose recorded opportunity.state is ENTER YES or ENTER NO create a paper order; WATCH and other states create no order but remain in probability evidence
execution.side: opportunity.side as chosen by the engine (YES or NO); YES uses yes_ask and yes_ask_size, NO uses no_ask and no_ask_size
execution.snapshot_window: the fill snapshot is the execution snapshot for the same market_id with the EARLIEST observed_at satisfying executable_after <= observed_at <= executable_after + maximum_input_age_seconds, observed_at <= min(expires_at, observation_end_at) - decision_costs.minimum_seconds_to_expiry (remaining entry horizon at execution >= 300 seconds) and observed_at <= report_as_of
execution.same_timestamp: snapshots sharing that earliest observed_at count once when identical in every field; if they differ in any quote or size the order is a nonfill (reason: execution_snapshot_conflict), never an order-dependent choice
execution.no_search: later snapshots are never searched for a better price; if the fill snapshot lacks a valid side ask (reason: side_ask_unavailable), has zero side ask size (reason: insufficient_liquidity), has non-finite, out-of-range or crossed quotes (reason: invalid_execution_snapshot), or fails the price limit (reason: limit_exceeded), the order is a nonfill
execution.nonfill: no snapshot inside snapshot_window is a nonfill (reason: no_execution_snapshot); fills are never assumed
execution.quote_preservation: the chosen snapshot's yes_bid, yes_ask, no_bid, no_ask, yes_ask_size, no_ask_size and observed_at are all recorded unchanged in the decision output, together with the decision-time quotes
execution.price_limit: fill only if conservative_probability - effective_cost - scenario resolution_haircut >= decision_costs.min_conservative_edge, where effective_cost = all_in_cost(1 unit) at the later side ask, i.e. the engine's whole-contract (Kalshi) candidate cost with the cent-rounded fee (reason: limit_exceeded)
execution.quantity: intended units = largest whole number of contracts whose all-in cost at the later side ask is <= opportunity.suggested_max_exposure; filled units = min(intended units, floor(max_volume_participation * later side ask size)) further limited by the remaining max_event_bankroll_fraction * paper_bankroll event exposure, processed in (decision time, observation_id) order; 0 filled units is a nonfill (reason: insufficient_liquidity) and fewer than intended is a partial fill
execution.all_in_cost: units * ask * (1 + fee_rate + scenario slippage_bps / 10000) + units * scenario fee_multiplier * fee_coefficient * ask * (1 - ask), with the fee rounded up to the cent as in CryptoThresholdEngine.all_in_cost
execution.settlement: per filled contract, payout is 1 if the chosen side wins else 0, minus scenario resolution_haircut; rows unresolved at report_as_of are open and unscored
